decisions.reason: The print-production condition does not change the already-active digital flipbook deliverable; the source explicitly distinguishes the Flip Book from the conditional print version.
Making print production conditional does not alter the requirement to remediate low-quality article images.
The article-end whitespace policy remains applicable to the magazine layout regardless of whether a print version is produced.
The conditional print decision does not change which cover-listed articles must be included in the magazine.
The source does not relax or otherwise change the requirement that advertisements render sharply in the magazine.
The magazine's polished, brand-aligned visual style remains required independently of conditional print production.
The print-production condition has no effect on the established red-usage policy.
The magazine still requires a compiled and formatted layout for the digital flipbook; only production of the separate print-ready output becomes conditional.
The source decision does not change the specified website as the source for magazine articles.
Conditional print production does not alter the approved article body typeface, readability constraint, or font weight.
The future word-count guidance concerns avoiding layout whitespace and is unaffected by whether printed copies are requested.
The table of contents must still match finalized magazine pagination for the digital deliverable; the conditional print decision does not change that requirement.
